data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism's concluding assertion — 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all' — is a non sequitur that contradicts the very evolutionary model it invokes. The described mechanism shifts rationality to population-level selection, but evolutionary selection requires a variation pool from which to select. That variation pool is generated by individual scientists' cognitive processes. If the 'underlying structure' of individual reasoning shapes which candidate theories enter the pool (the 'blind variation' input), then that structure is causally relevant to the outcome — it constrains the search space the selective filter operates on. An evolutionary-selection account therefore entails that the underlying structure of individual agency IS relevant to the outcome (it determines the variation distribution), not that it was 'never relevant.' The target's own mechanism thus undermines its own conclusion, making the dissolution internally incoherent.
